Q: uninstall openjdk in mac A:

A JDK can be installed anywhere on your Mac, not just /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines.

which java

In Terminal.app (or any such console), type and execute:

which java

You will see the path to the java executable.

Q: SymPy .equals() in combination with parse_latex() not giving the same results as .equals() without parsing? A: 
from sympy import *
from sympy.parsing.latex import parse_latex
pef = parse_latex(r"\sin(\pi/2)")
pef.has(pi)
# False
srepr(pef)
# "sin(Mul(Symbol('pi'), Pow(Integer(2), Integer(-1))))"

As you can see, parse_latex parsed r"\pi" into a symbol. That's why the sin function doesn't evaluate.

Looking at parse_latex documentation, I don't see any keyword argument that would help us tell it to parse r"\pi" into pi, which is a number. One way to achieve the desired result is to post process the output of parse_latex:

d = {
    Symbol("pi"): pi
}
pef = pef.subs(d)
pef
# 1

Q: How do I write a type hint to indicate that a variable is a specific subtype of the return type of a method A:

Use typing.cast when the runtime subtype is known

If you are certain that some_object.method() will always return B in your specific context, the idiomatic way to inform the type checker without using assert is typing.cast.

cast is a static typing construct: it affects only the type checker and has no effect at runtime.

from typing import cast

class MyClass:
    def __init__(self):
        variable = cast(B, some_object.method())
        self.attribute = variable

This tells tools like mypy or pyright to treat the value as B, even though the declared return type is A.

When to use this

  • Use assert isinstance(...) if you want a runtime check.

  • Use cast(...) if the subtype is guaranteed by external logic and you only need to narrow the type for static analysis.

cast is appropriate here because the type narrowing is based on contextual knowledge that the type checker cannot infer.

Q: Playwright Allure Report in Email A:

Since you are probably attempting to email the html file only instead of the whole dir that's why the content seems broken.

Try using the --single-file option that will embed all required assets in one single file as its name suggests. Is there a way to export Allure Report to a single html file? To share with the team

Otherwise you'd need to zip the whole allure-report and send it via email.. the receiver will just need to unpack it and open the html file locally.

zip -r allure-report.zip allure-report

Q: What additional fields are needed to identify instances of services in metrics, traces, logs - After replicating services across multiple replicas? A:

The HOSTNAME variable is set by Docker and is a unique ID per container. If you list the environment variables with docker run --rm debian env you'll see that the HOSTNAME is something like 846772ae945f and changes every time you run the command and create a new container.
